newsitem.title: DUBAI: Khashoggi threatens steps over Thai charges-paper.
newsitem.headline: Khashoggi threatens steps over Thai charges-paper.

text.p: Saudi tycoon Adnan Khashoggi will take legal action against Thai authorities if they did not drop charges against him, a newspaper reported on Thursday.

"Khashoggi asserted that he is in the process of taking legal measures against the Thai authorities if they do not put a stop to accusations against him," the London-based Arabic-language Asharq al-Awsat newspaper said.
An arrest warrant was issued last week by Thai police for Khashoggi, 61, wanted on charges of conspiring to defraud the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.
On Wednesday, Thai police said they had frozen shares worth 142 million baht ($5.5 million) held by Khashoggi in Thai firm Jalaprathan Cement Plc.
Speaking to Asharq al-Awsat from Paris, Khashoggi said freezing his shares in the cement firm would "hasten the collapse of the company".
"He said the loans he had obtained from Thailand were still there in Bangkok through various investments. (He) denied that these investments might be frozen," it added.

The arrest warrant for Khashoggi and four other officials of the troubled bank was issued at the request of the Thai central bank on suspicion they jointly conspired for Khashoggi to draw two billion baht in loans from Bangkok Bank of Commerce in 1995 without credible collateral.
The globe-trotting Saudi businessman's multi-million dollar deals, court cases and elite acquaintances have spread his fame throughout the world.

Bangkok Bank of Commerce, saddled with non-performing loans of more than 70 billion baht, was taken over by the government last year after opposition charges about the debts triggered a run on deposits.
